nom: Paula's Choice 25% Vitamin C + Glutathione Clinical Serum

avis.titre: Nothing remarkable, cheaper and more effective options are available
avis.texte: I only gave this 3 stars because while my skin didn’t improve, it didn’t get worse. I was using a different brand that I got good results from. I like that it wasn’t too tacky, the good news is that it doesn’t pill. It went on smoothly which is important if you are layering your products.

I have extremely sensitive, acne-prone skin and use tretinoin, so finding a vitamin C that doesn’t irritate my skin has been a challenge. This is the only vitamin C I’ve found that is both gentle and effective. It has noticeably brightened my skin without causing redness, stinging, or breakouts. If you have sensitive skin and have struggled with other vitamin C products, I highly recommend giving this one a try.
An excellent choice for sensitive skin. Very expensive but you can find it on sale if you are vigilant.
This my 2nd bottle purchase. I love that this has 25% vitamin C. It made my skin look brighter and younger.
Love this formula! Definately evens out skin tone. Has helped with some irritated/ discolored spots on my face. Not heavy. Very nice.

Ordered my second bottle, the first lasted 3 months. I use it in the morning after cleansing, toner & BHA, followed up with spf moisture. I'm 48f w/oily, acne prone skin & this routine is giving real results. I'm going days w/out makeup and haven't felt confidant enough to do that in a long time. I also started tretinoin in February but I use that at night after toner. I eased into the tret with minimal irritation. I think that's because I had used Paula's Choice Retinol at night for years prior but now need something stronger due to hormonal changes. Sorry for the novel. I've struggled but have found Paula's Choice skincare products really helpful & hope this will help someone else;)

I’ve always used a vitamin c serum in my skincare routine and this one is one of my favorites that I’ve tried! I like that it’s clinical strength, so you know it’s actually going to work. It also comes in a pump style bottle, making it easy to disperse the product. I use it in the morning and follow it up with a SPF to protect my skin. I find that the serum looks great under makeup and doesn’t pill at all. It also has a creamy look, but once spread out you can’t see it on your skin. Over time, it has done a good job of brightening my skin and lightening up any dark spots. It is a bit pricey though, so you could just use it on the areas you want to target. However, I like to use it everywhere to give a brighter look to my entire face. My one wish is for the bottle to be see through, so you could see how much product you have left.

This vitamin C serum by Paula’s Choice has a slightly creamy quality to it and applies beautifully to my skin. I like that this is a 25% formula that doesn’t cause irritation and also feels quite nice on my skin. The only thing is that I’ve seemed to go through the bottle rather quickly as it seems to require a bit more product to spread over my face and neck than a lightweight gel serum. I really like the product, it just doesn’t seem to be lasting as long. And since it’s not a low priced serum, the speed through which I’m going through the bottle might deter me from repurchasing it in the future.

Very simply: this is a Vitamin C stabilized by additional ingredients. It should have a long shelf-life. So why am I receiving a product that expires in 8 months? It should be MY choice to use any unopened skincare product for at least a year. This is the earliest expiry I've ever gotten on Vitamin C. Maybe it's not as stable as its brand brags.

As a mature woman, I look for Vitamin C in my skin care products because I feel it makes a difference in the appearance of my skin. This is a light, white lotion that is 25% Vitamin C, which is more than any other similar product I have used. I detect no scent when I apply this lotion, and it is immediately absorbed into my skin, leaving no sticky or greasy feeling. It only needs to be applied once a day after cleansing, toning and exfoliating. As suggested, I follow it up with sunscreen every day for maximum protection from the elements. I like everything about this Paula's Choice Serum from the small pump bottle which dispenses just the right amount without contaminating the rest to the fantastic way it makes my skin appear brighter and smoother. This is definitely my new favorite.

I ordered this bottle of Paula’s choice face serum, because I have a lot of sun damage to reverse on my face. This bottle contains 25% vitamin C, and it is very easy to apply in the morning and at night. It dispenses easily and is not sticky. It absorbs well and is very moisturizing. I will continue using this and I am looking forward to seeing the results of this product.

I purchased this on a recommendation. While I enjoyed the product, I would not purchase again due to the misleading packaging. While the bottle does not lie, there is only 1 ounce, most buyers would not notice the amount and look to the bottle size for quantity. I typically open packaging up to get the last bit I can while new product is on the way. Imagine my surprise when I tried to open this one! I first noticed how difficult it was to open. I had to saw it open with a steak knife. My first thought was that the bottle was extra thick so less space was available for the product. Imagine my surprise when I opened it to find the the bottle had NOTHING IN IT! The hole in the bottom portion confirmed that claim. The entire bottom was simply an airless pump for the measly product located in the top. I will not purchace this product again.

Has it been oxidized? I bought it because of the claim that the active ingredients, vitamin C derivatives, can have a longer shelf life and can withstand oxidation better than ascorbic acid (vitamin C). Yet when I started using my third bottle, the cream turned out to be yellowish instead of white. I suspected that it had been oxidized. It made me question why I should have paid a premium for a vitamin C derivatives cream. I will switch to a cheap vitamin C serum.
I have this in a sample size and liked it enough to buy a bigger bottle. Now $60.00 and I still get a small bottle. As much as I like this product will not buy again.

I started using this on my entire face initially, but ended up using it only where I have sun spots under my eyes. I have been using the serum for about a month and can see a noticeable difference. The skin where the serum has been applied is much brighter and the sun spots are lighter. I think I will start applying to my entire face again, and would repurchase if the same differences are seen.
